title: Critical Response Tactics for Responding to a Home Intruder
summary: Learn critical home defense tactics for responding to a home intruder, including situational awareness, positioning, escape strategies, and Byrna less-lethal options.
body_markdown:
## Home Defense Tips: How to Prepare Your Home with Byrna


When it comes to home defense,[having the right tools](https://byrna.com/collections/byrna-non-lethal-guns) is only part of the equation. Knowing how to use those tools and preparing before an emergency can help homeowners respond more effectively if a threat enters the home.


One important consideration is where self-defense tools are stored. Firearms should be secured appropriately and kept away from immediate reach, particularly in the bedroom where someone may be disoriented after waking. Less-lethal options such as a Byrna launcher can provide another option for an immediate response while remaining part of a broader home-defense strategy.


A


flashlight is another useful addition to a home safety plan. Keeping one readily accessible can help illuminate dark areas while moving through the home and may also serve as a distraction device.


### Use Awareness and Distance to Your Advantage


If an intruder enters the home, awareness and positioning can be critical. Homeowners should consider announcing their presence and making it clear that someone is home. Many burglars are looking for an unoccupied house and may leave once they realize someone is present.


Movement through the home should prioritize distance and visibility. When approaching corners or doorways, using angles can help provide a better view before entering an area. A basic threshold evaluation can also help identify potential hazards before moving through a doorway.


Reflective surfaces, including mirrors, window panes, and picture frames, may provide additional visibility around corners or through doorways.


### The Goal Is Getting to Safety


Home defense is ultimately about protecting people rather than confronting an intruder. At the first safe opportunity, calling 911 and clearly communicating the location and situation should be a priority.


A well-rounded home safety plan combines preparation, awareness, responsible storage, training, and appropriate self-defense options. With these elements in place, homeowners can be better prepared to protect themselves and their families while creating opportunities to escape and seek help when necessary.
